newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso dives on interest rates, scandal.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso dives on interest rates, scandal.

text.p: BOGOTA, Aug 19 Reuter - Colombia's peso fell 7.45 pesos to close at 1,137.5 against the dollar Tuesday in the wake of a drop in interest rates and a brewing political scandal involving two government ministers, interbank traders said.
The peso opened at 1,131 and sank to an intraday low of 1,141. Traders reported a total of 275 deals for a total $140 million.

Markets were closed for a national holiday Monday and so were reacting for the first time Tuesday to the central bank decision, announced Friday, to shave 0.5 percent off overnight deposit rates. The central bank rate now stands at 20 percent for overnight deposits and 27 percent for overnight lending.

Traders also said markets got the jitters in the face of allegations published in the weekly political magazine Semana that Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar and Communications Minister Saulo Arboleda may have illegally awarded a number of new radio broadcast licenses.
The authorities have launched a criminal investigation into the claims and President Ernesto Samper's cabinet was meeting Tuesday to consider whether to force the two officials to resign.
"There were no export earnings from the coffee or oil industries coming into the market. Industry was looking for dollars and banks were looking to build up positions," a trader said.
"The political scandal is also affecting the situation because it generates instability."
